title: Clay, Fire, Air, and Mostly Water: Understanding the Importance of Water Resources in Pottery Workshops in Ancient Iberia by Integrating Ethnoarchaeological, Experimental, and Archaeological Research

supports: 2018 participant observation at Padilla Herrera brothers' Bailen workshop: initial shade and avoiding strong drafts; sun only near dry. Seasonal drying described as summer 3–4 days, spring/autumn 6–7 days.

doesNotVerify: No matched pot wall/capacity/density/weather/mass time series for those day ranges. No crack probabilities. Wheel throwing differs from untempered island coil pots. Article mass-loss discussion includes firing; do not infer ordinary drying mass or density from it.

evidence.shortExcerpt: Generally, in summer, drying requires 3–4 days, and in spring or autumn, drying requires 6–7 days.
